prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: Across the five frames, the camera wearer turns from a view into a small room toward a nearby wall or doorway and then toward a person partly entering at the far right. The first two frames suggest room surfaces roughly 1–3 m away, with furniture or objects farther ahead; the third and fourth frames place a broad wall-like surface very close, approximately 0.3–1 m in front, while darker regions indicate more distant or unresolved space. In the fifth frame, the bright facial region at the upper right appears within roughly 0.3–0.7 m, partly out of view, with darker bedding or furniture behind it around 1–2 m away; no reliable facing or gaze direction can be recovered from depth alone. The map makes near-versus-far surfaces and the rapid approach or turn toward the wall and person clearer than RGB, but its large smooth gradients, black regions, and implausibly merged boundaries make metric distances, occlusions, and distances between individual objects unreliable.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map marks only two adjacent regions in the second frame, labeling a large central-left mask as "cat" and a smaller mask immediately to its right as "banana"; both appear roughly 1–2 m ahead and near each other, with the larger region extending from near the top to the lower part of the frame. These masks do not correspond convincingly to clearly identifiable objects in the RGB, so their classes, shapes, relative distance, and apparent partial overlap or adjacency are unreliable. Frames one and three through five contain no masks, leaving the room surfaces, furniture, nearby wall, and partially visible person at the right edge spatially unresolved. The map could make object extent and occlusion boundaries clearer than RGB when correct, but here it misses the visible person and most scene elements and provides no dependable evidence about gaze, facing direction, reachability, or motion across frames.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is entirely black in all five frames, so it detects no body or hand skeletons and supplies no joint positions, facing directions, gaze cues, or reach relationships. It therefore cannot spatially locate the partially visible person in the fifth RGB frame, whose face is close to the camera at the upper-right edge and partly outside the field of view, nor can it establish whether any other person is present in earlier frames. No approach, retreat, turning, limb motion, or person-to-object distance can be tracked from this map. A valid pose map could reveal articulated body and hand geometry that is difficult to see in blurred or occluded RGB frames, but this output is unreliable because it contains no detections.
